subject: Cloud Computing
title: Regional Cloud Champions
description: A quick win: understand Regional Cloud Champions.

hook.text: Not every country trusts American cloud providers. Regional champions serve local markets worldwide.

buildup.text: OVHcloud dominates in France. Yandex Cloud serves Russia. Tencent and Huawei compete in China.

discovery.text: Data sovereignty laws force some customers to use local providers. Their data must stay in-country.

twist.text: Regional providers can't match the big three in features. But compliance requirements make them essential.

climax.text: The cloud market isn't one global contest. It's dozens of local battles with different winners in each.

punchline.text: Global cloud has local rules. Local players know them best.

quiz.question: Why do regional cloud providers survive against the global giants?
options: Data sovereignty laws often require local data storage and processing
Regional providers always have better technology than AWS
Global cloud providers refuse to serve small countries

details.summary: Regional cloud providers like OVHcloud in Europe, Yandex Cloud in Russia, and Naver Cloud in South Korea serve local markets with data sovereignty compliance, local language support, and competitive regional pricing. They compete by serving needs that global hyperscalers address less effectively.
details.whyItMatters: Not all cloud computing is dominated by US hyperscalers. Regional providers serve important roles in data sovereignty, local compliance, and economic independence from American tech giants.
takeaways: Regional providers offer local data sovereignty compliance
They serve markets where hyperscalers face regulatory barriers
Local language and support create customer loyalty

faq.question: Why do regional cloud providers exist?
faq.answer: Data sovereignty laws require data to remain in specific countries. Some organizations prefer providers under local jurisdiction. Regional providers offer local language support, regional pricing, and understanding of local regulatory requirements that global providers may not prioritize.

faq.question: Can regional providers compete with hyperscalers?
faq.answer: They compete effectively in their local markets, especially for workloads with sovereignty requirements. However, they cannot match the service breadth, global reach, or R&D investment of AWS, Azure, and GCP. Many customers use regional providers alongside hyperscalers.
